text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

An all-woman panel selecting a woman over another woman tells you essentially nothing about sex discrimination — both candidates shared the same sex, so sex can't explain the difference between you. Panel composition also varies for mundane reasons: who was available, departmental gender balance, deliberate balance requirements. Raising it would likely read as a grievance about the panel's identity rather than the decision, and would weaken your credible complaint.

Your real issue is procedural: the shortlisted candidate appears less qualified on formal criteria, and you've had no written justification after two weeks. Most public universities owe you reasons and have a fixed deadline. Send a written follow-up citing the relevant rules, request the scoring against published criteria, and note your appeal deadline.
